Toll booths are a usage fee and are an almost perfect example of taxation as representation because they only levy the tax on those who choose to utilize the infrastructure that the tax is paying for. A large part of the reason for tolls is when metropolitan areas straddle state lines and a large number of the people using a road do not reside in the borders of the state that is paying for it.

Look at NYC and NJ/CT/PA as an example. If the state of New York is using gas taxes and income taxes to fund highways, workers who live out of state, but routinely commute into New York, but always buy gas out of state because it's cheaper (due to lower gas taxes) then they are placing a heavy usage burden on the roads being paid for by New York state, but those users are contributing nothing to pay for those roads. The toll booths extract revenue from those users. If not for toll booths then the taxes in New York state would have to be higher to subsidize the road usage for drivers from NJ CT and PA.

Every state with a large city near the border has the same issues and often looks to toll booths to extract revenue from the out of state users.
